text:
Anya: heads up — noticed p95 drift on /generate-route after the kernel handoff in staging
Mike: rough numbers?
Anya: short prompts (<64 tokens) p95 from ~180ms -> ~320ms across the cluster for ~8min window
Sophie: did KV hitrate change at the same time?
Anya: yes, kv hitrate down ~12% (staging metrics) and KV lookup latency +~3ms
Rafael: that lines up with the fast-attn->attention-opt-x switchover we flipped at 03:01
Mike: hmm, attention-opt-x has different memory layout; could affect cache locality and kernel prefetch behavior
Sophie: could also be queueing — were large requests allowed to cut ahead?
Anya: scheduler logs show a few bursts where 1k-token requests got pulled into microbatches early, pushing small requests out
Mike: thinking: enforce p95-driven token budgets by route/tier. e.g. max_budget {free:16, standard:64, pro:96} and refuse/buffer beyond that for p95-critical routes
Sophie: + kernel selection policy: prefer kernel-A for seq<128, kernel-B for seq>=128. That way microbatch shapes stay friendly to KV cache and prefetch heuristics
Rafael: tried a quick local canary yesterday: set token budgets free=16,std=64,pro=96 + kernel routing by seq len -> staging p95 back to ~190ms for short prompts
perf-bot: PERF PROFILE: cpu_ms +24% on softmax path during handoff; kv_lookup median +3ms; scheduler queue-depth spiked from 6 -> 14 during incident window
Mike: good to have numbers. Also noticed microbatch formation time increased slightly when kernel changed — kernel init paths touching new kernel warmed slower
Sophie: two levers: (1) token-budget gating per route/tier, (2) queue reorder by effective_token_cost (small requests prioritized), (3) kernel affinity by seq len
Anya: I prototyped a comparator for reordering: 
```py
# comparator: lower cost = higher priority
def cost_key(req):
    return req.tokens / max(1, req.priority_weight)
```
Rafael: reorder + token budgets in the canary cut p95 tail, KV hit recovered a bit (within 2%) — suggests burst mixing was the main culprit
Mike: rollout plan idea: night canary on 10% of dedicated nodes -> run for 2h, monitor p95, kv_hit, cpu_ms, kernel-init failures
Sophie: add a metric alert for p95 > 250ms and kv_hit drop > 6% during canary window
Anya: I'll open an RFC with the proposed canary config + scheduler patch + kernel-affinity table. Will attach perf diffs and flame graphs
Mike: also include a fallback: if p95 spikes we auto-fallback to previous kernel and revert token-budget changes for that route-tier
Rafael: will help test kernel-affinity rules and add microbenchmarks for kernel warm paths
Sophie: ping me when RFC lands, I'll review scheduler and rollout steps
Anya: thanks — creating RFC and will drop the link here when done :thumbsup:
Mike: cool, thanks everyone
perf-bot: deploy-bot: canary job queued on cluster-dedicated-3 (runbook: /runbooks/latency-trimming-mini-batcher)
Anya: noted — will follow the runbook during cutover and post results here
